**My pick for the best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900 is the <Entity category="product" value="BLUETTI AC200L"/>**, particularly if you want to plug your RV directly into the power station.

  <box flex="1" gap={1}>

    <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums={true}>$854.05</title>

    <badge color="success">Best overall for RV hookup</badge>
    <text size="sm">2,048Wh LiFePO4 battery · 2,400W AC output · Built-in TT-30 RV outlet · 1,200W solar input</text>

  </box>

The supplied Dealectric result reports that the discount code was tested on November 2, 2026. I haven't independently verified today's checkout price. <Cite ref="turn380068view0"/>

## Other strong options under $900

| Model | Listed price | Capacity | Why consider it |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO** | $676.16 | 2,048Wh | Best budget value with TT-30 outlet |
| **OUPES Mega 2 Pro** | $699 | 2,048Wh | 2,500W output and expandable capacity |
| **Renogy PowerStation 2000** | $799 | 2,048Wh | TT-30 outlet and UPS functionality |
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | $854.05 with code | 2,048Wh | Strong RV features and solar charging |

Prices are from the provided October–November 2026 search results and may change. <Cite ref="turn380068view0"/>

## Important RV considerations

A 30A RV outlet doesn't necessarily provide 30A of usable power. The AC200L's 2,400W inverter supplies approximately **20A at 120V**, so it can handle many RV essentials, but not necessarily a rooftop air conditioner alongside other heavy loads.

Also, your RV's converter can consume significant energy charging its house battery, and an absorption refrigerator running on electricity can drain a 2kWh station quickly.

**Bottom line:** Choose the **BLUETTI AC200L at $854.05** for its RV-friendly setup and solar capability. If price matters most, the **Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO at $676.16** is a compelling alternative with similar battery capacity and AC output.

One question would help narrow this down: **Do you need to run your RV's rooftop air conditioner, or mainly the fridge, lights, water pump, and electronics?**
